description: C as the language of the machine: types, pointers, memory, structures, files and the toolchain, taught by writing and debugging real systems-style programs. Taught to the depth of a leading systems programming course.
modelledOn: Kernighan and Ritchie, The C Programming Language
Bryant and O'Hallaron, Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (C and memory chapters)
King, C Programming: A Modern Approach
outcomes: Write well-structured C programs using the full type system, operators, control flow and functions.
Use arrays, strings and pointers correctly and explain their representation in memory.
Allocate and free dynamic memory and build linked structures without leaks or dangling pointers.
Model data with structures, unions and enumerations and persist it with text and binary files.
Drive the preprocessor, compiler, linker and debugger, and split a program across multiple files.
Find memory errors with tools such as a debugger and a sanitizer and reason about undefined behaviour.

units.title: C syntax, types and operators
topics: A first program; compiling with gcc or clang; the structure of a C program
Integer, character and floating types; sizes, ranges, signedness, overflow, limits.h
Constants, variables, declarations, initialisation; const and typedef
Arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise and assignment operators; precedence; implicit conversions
printf and scanf formatting; getchar and putchar

units.title: Control flow and functions
topics: if, switch, while, do-while, for; break, continue, goto
Function definition and declaration, prototypes, header files
Call by value; scope, storage classes (auto, static, extern, register)
Recursion and the call stack; stack frames
Modular design: splitting a program into functions and files

units.title: Arrays and strings
topics: One- and multi-dimensional arrays; initialisation; array bounds and the danger of overrun
Strings as null-terminated char arrays; string.h functions and writing your own strlen, strcpy, strcmp
Passing arrays to functions; sizeof pitfalls
Sorting and searching arrays; a word-count and a Caesar cipher program

units.title: Pointers and memory
topics: Addresses, the & and * operators, pointer types, NULL
Pointer arithmetic and the equivalence of arrays and pointers; pointers to pointers
Call by reference with pointers; returning multiple values; swap
The memory map of a process: text, data, BSS, heap, stack
Dynamic memory: malloc, calloc, realloc, free; leaks, double free, use after free
Linked lists, stacks and a binary tree with dynamic nodes
Function pointers and callbacks; qsort

units.title: Structures, unions and enumerations
topics: Defining and using struct; nested structures; arrays of structures; the arrow operator
Memory layout, padding and alignment
Unions and tagged unions; bit fields; enum
Structures as records: a student register and an inventory program

units.title: File handling
topics: Streams: stdin, stdout, stderr; fopen, fclose and modes
Text I/O: fgets, fputs, fprintf, fscanf; line-by-line processing
Binary I/O: fread, fwrite, fseek, ftell; writing and reading records
Error handling with errno and perror; checking return values
Command-line arguments and processing a CSV file of sales data

units.title: The preprocessor and compilation
topics: #include, #define, macros with arguments and their pitfalls, conditional compilation, include guards
The pipeline: preprocessing, compilation, assembly, linking; object files and libraries
Makefiles and building multi-file projects; static and shared libraries
Compiler flags, warnings as errors and optimisation levels

units.title: Debugging, safety and undefined behaviour
topics: gdb: breakpoints, stepping, inspecting memory and the stack
AddressSanitizer and Valgrind for leaks and invalid accesses
Undefined behaviour: uninitialised variables, signed overflow, buffer overflow and why it matters for security
Defensive coding, assertions and unit tests in C
Project: a small system utility or data manager combining files, structs and pointers

schedule.title: First programs and types
schedule.exercise: Write, compile and run a program that prints the size and range of each basic type, and explain in two sentences what happens when an int overflows.

tasks.title: Compile and run a hello program with gcc, then add a second function and observe the compiler error when its prototype is missing
Print sizeof and the limits.h range of every integer type, then demonstrate unsigned wraparound and signed overflow on a 16-bit value
Write a temperature table program using constants, typedef and floating point, and show a precision bug caused by integer division

schedule.title: Operators and formatted I/O
schedule.exercise: Problem set: predict the output of ten expressions mixing operators and conversions, then check each by running it.

tasks.title: Evaluate ten arithmetic and bitwise expressions by hand using precedence rules and confirm each result by running the program
Write a program that sets, clears and toggles bits in an 8-bit register value using masks and prints the results in binary
Read a price and quantity with scanf, handle bad input by checking the return value, and print a formatted receipt with aligned columns

schedule.title: Control flow and functions
schedule.exercise: Write a menu-driven calculator with separate functions, then explain how arguments are copied on each call.

tasks.title: Write a program using for and while loops to print the multiplication table and the first 20 Fibonacci numbers
Split a prime-checking program into a header, an implementation file and a main file, and compile all three together
Demonstrate call by value with a failed swap function, then use static and global variables to count function calls and explain scope

schedule.title: Recursion and modular design
schedule.exercise: Trace the call stack for a recursive factorial of 5 on paper and design the file layout for a small calculator project.

tasks.title: Step through a recursive factorial of 5 and record the stack frames as they are pushed and popped
Write recursive functions for Fibonacci and binary search, count the calls each makes and show an overflow of the stack with a missing base case
Split a 150-line program into modules with clear interfaces, then compile it with separate object files and check no function is defined twice

schedule.title: Arrays and strings
schedule.exercise: Implement your own strlen, strcpy and strcmp, and test them against the library versions on edge cases.

tasks.title: Fill an array with ten marks, compute the mean and maximum, and show what happens when the loop runs one element past the end
Write your own strlen, strcpy and strcmp and test each against the standard library on empty strings and long inputs
Write a Caesar cipher and a word counter that read text from input, and sort the words by frequency with a function you write

schedule.title: Pointers
schedule.exercise: Draw a memory diagram of three pointer variables and an array and trace pointer arithmetic on it.

tasks.title: Declare an int, a pointer to it and a pointer to the pointer, then follow the arrows on the memory view and print each address
Rewrite array indexing as pointer arithmetic and walk an integer array with a pointer, verifying that a[i] equals *(a+i)
Write functions that return the minimum, maximum and mean of an array through pointer parameters, and a swap that actually works

schedule.title: Memory map and dynamic memory
schedule.exercise: Label the segments of a process memory map for a small program and list where each of its variables lives.

tasks.title: Locate a global, a static, a local and a malloc'd variable in the process memory map and print their addresses to confirm the layout
Allocate and resize an array of student marks with malloc and realloc, and free it with no leak, checking each return value
Fix a program with a memory leak, a double free and a use after free, and prove it is clean with a debug tool

schedule.title: Linked structures and function pointers
schedule.exercise: Draw the diagram for inserting and deleting a node in a linked list, and explain how qsort uses a comparison callback.

tasks.title: Build a singly linked list with insert-at-head and print it, stepping the visualiser to see each pointer change
Implement a stack with a linked list and a binary search tree with insert and in-order traversal, freeing every node at exit
Sort an array of structs with qsort using function pointers for three different keys, then write a table-driven menu using an array of function pointers

schedule.title: Structures, unions and enums
schedule.exercise: Design a record layout for a student register and explain the size reported by sizeof for each field order.

tasks.title: Define a student struct with name, index number and marks, fill an array of five and print them using the arrow operator
Print offsetof and sizeof for a struct, reorder its fields to remove padding and show that the size shrinks
Build an inventory program with structs, enums for category and a union for variable data, with add, search and report functions

schedule.title: Files and records
schedule.exercise: Design a record file format for a student register and describe how you would detect a corrupted record.

tasks.title: Open a text file with fopen, write ten lines with fprintf, close it and read them back, checking that every call succeeded
Read a text file line by line with fgets, parse the fields with sscanf and report the lines that are malformed
Write an array of structs to a binary file and update the fifth record in place with fseek, then read the file back and verify it

schedule.title: Error handling and the CSV project
schedule.exercise: Write a usage message and error table for a command-line tool that summarises sales by region from a CSV file.

tasks.title: Open a file that does not exist, print the error with errno and perror, and exit with a non-zero status
Read a CSV of sales from a file named on the command line and print totals per region, rejecting rows with the wrong number of fields
Write a robust CSV summary tool that handles missing files, quoted fields, empty lines and very long lines without crashing, and test it on five bad inputs

schedule.title: Preprocessor, compilation and building
schedule.exercise: Write a Makefile for a three-file project that builds a static library and a program, and explain each linking step.

tasks.title: Write a macro to square a number, show how it breaks with the argument a+b, and fix it with parentheses and an inline function
Write a Makefile that builds a three-file program and rebuilds only the changed file, then run make twice and observe the output
Compile a program in four separate stages with gcc flags, inspect the assembly and object file, and link a static library into the final binary

schedule.title: Debugging, safety and the project
schedule.exercise: Project plan: specify a small data manager utility, its tests, its error handling and a safety checklist for it.

tasks.title: Run a program in gdb, set a breakpoint, step through a loop and print a variable and the call stack at a chosen line
Find and fix an off-by-one buffer overflow, an uninitialised variable and a signed overflow in a given program, using AddressSanitizer output
Build a small data manager combining files, structs and dynamic lists, then test it with assertions and a leak checker and fix every defect found
